A command-line tool just made NIP-65 relay selection and NIP-02 petname paths scriptable, and the release notes say nothing about either.

nak v0.21.0 was tagged on 3 October 2026 with an empty release body, so the seventeen commits since v0.20.7 are the only account of it. Two matter. A new relays subcommand prints the NIP-65 relays for a pubkey, one per line, with --inbox/--read and --outbox/--write filters. Petname path resolution moved into the shared pubkey parser, so anything beginning with a tilde resolves anywhere a pubkey is accepted, including the mixed form ~erin@names.com/david/frank.

The filter detail is the one worth knowing: --inbox --outbox is an AND, not a union. It prints only relays serving both directions, which under NIP-65 is what an unmarked r tag produces.

We read the diff when the release notes are empty, because on this release the version number and the changelog tell you nothing. The absolute-root rule is the practical catch: a path rooted in a hex pubkey, a NIP-05 identifier or an npub resolves with no key, while a path starting from your own follows asks for a signer. Do you know which of those your scripts rely on?

None of this changes a specification. It is a tool catching up to NIP-02 and NIP-65 as they already stand, and a relay list still guides routing without proving any relay accepted anything.

nak v0.21.0, tagged 3 October 2026, ships with an empty release body. The seventeen commits since v0.20.7 are the only account of it.

Two additions: a relays subcommand that prints a pubkey's NIP-65 relays one per line, filtered by --inbox/--read and --outbox/--write, and NIP-02 petname resolution moved into the shared pubkey parser, so a leading tilde works anywhere a pubkey is accepted.

Watch the filter: --inbox --outbox requires both marks on the same relay, not either. That is what an unmarked r tag produces.

Absolute roots (hex pubkey, NIP-05 identifier, npub, nprofile) resolve without a key. A relative path starting from your own follows needs a signer.
